const p="/Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/req-029/tmp/req-029-product-baseline.md";const body=`# REQ-029 Mesh Talk product baseline and candidate backlog

Committed source examined is \`req-029\` at \`0ae1a69261c3fca12bad8bb62021f5fce8d6db2c\` (2026-11-22). The workspace version is \`0.4.6\` and identifies the source target. Published versions and availability were outside this local audit. Findings come from committed code, guides and Git history. Existing evidence below retains the scope recorded by its owners. This audit ran no builds, tests, native scenarios, live API calls or deployments. [Workspace version](../Cargo.toml#L13) · [Implementation status](../specifications/TODO.md#current-capability-areas)

## Requirement provenance and authority

- \`e5133000\` (#380) consolidated the 30 inputs into REQ, WORK and T entries. \`5fe57c38\` superseded T-number sequencing with a foundation-first plan. \`6b28c838\` retired the roadmap and its assignment rules. Cite historical IDs as provenance for a candidate. Use the current capability index for implementation status, the module map for engineering ownership and the relevant feature guide for the governing contract. [Project index](../PROJECT.md#maintained-references) · [Documentation ownership](../docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) · [Module ownership](../docs/module-boundaries.md#2-feature-owners-and-shared-decisions)
- REQ-029 was peer-tool opportunity research (WORK-23/T069), with scenario-driven activation in the last roadmap. A useful peer precedent can motivate a candidate after the baseline comparison. Historical records do not establish current user demand, implementation approval or feature readiness. The original crosswalk is local via \`git show e5133000:docs/development-roadmap.md\` (lines 438–476), and its last form via \`git show 6b28c838^:docs/development-roadmap.md\` (lines 238–257 and 270–301). The deletion is visible with \`git show 6b28c838\`.
- Dedicated prior requirements are REQ-023 for existing-group voluntary voice, REQ-002 for browser content review, REQ-027 for mobile PWA, REQ-018 for independently governed personal/group synchronization, announcements and membership, REQ-013 for network exposure, REQ-025 for anti-harassment, and REQ-014 for comparable package size. File lifecycle draws on REQ-015/017/018, optional resource incentives on REQ-028, and manual image QR on REQ-010. Live screen sharing, anonymous chats, cross-device clipboard and message translation have no dedicated rows in that 30-item crosswalk. Treat them as candidate product decisions with the nearby contracts below.

## 1. Calls, video and screen sharing

- **At HEAD.** Experimental one-to-one desktop voice and video are off by default. The UI can target a contact, and a live signal addresses one device at a time. Each signal uses a fresh authenticated Noise/TCP connection. The call store owns a separate WebRTC peer connection with host-only ICE (\`iceServers: []\`) and non-trickle offer/answer gathering. Relay-only contacts fail the direct route requirement, and an existing routed VPN can work when both signaling and ICE media paths work. Signals have no durable mailbox path. Voice-only remote audio and camera failure fallback are implemented. Local device and loopback checks distinguish capture and actual received media. [Core signaling](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/call.rs#L52) · [Call store](../frontend/src/store/calls.ts#L192) · [Calls help](../docs/help/topics/calls.md) · [Network call flow](../docs/network-design-reference.md#f-calls-live-signaling-and-separate-media)
- **Evidence boundary.** The tracker records macOS Chromium to Windows Edge over Tailscale using real Noise signaling and decoded audio/video. It lists native macOS WebView calls and physical camera/microphone quality as separate gaps. The source includes browser readiness and physical media specs. [Evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker) · [Readiness spec](../frontend/e2e/call-readiness.spec.ts) · [Physical media spec](../frontend/e2e/call-media-physical.spec.ts)
- **Candidate slices.** Qualify existing 1:1 calls first with permission denial, route loss, sleep/reconnect and capture cleanup on target native hosts. Group voice is REQ-023 (WORK-16/T044–T045). The first slice was a voluntary voice session for accepted members of an existing group. The product and call owners still need to settle size, admission/revocation, initiator exit and audio controls. Group video and independent rooms were separate T046 decisions. Live screen sharing is a distinct candidate from screenshot capture and video attachments. The inspected call surface has no display capture, and the historical voice scope explicitly excluded it. A bounded first decision would specify source selection, OS permission denial, stop behavior and whether the first supported route is direct 1:1. TURN, remote reachability, recording and browser guests require their own scope and evidence. [Call ownership](../docs/module-boundaries.md#L88) · [Screenshot flow](../docs/help/topics/screenshots.md)

## 2. Files and folders

- **At HEAD.** Direct and group attachment flows cover files and folders with encrypted, signed chunks, durable exact-offer consent, integrity checks, retry and exact completion controls. The core file ceiling is 4 GiB with 48 KiB chunks, and directory packing adds caps of 10,000 entries, depth 32 and 1,024 path bytes. These are input ceilings. An offline path is eligible after the required encrypted chunks reach a surviving trusted holder within its bounds. Offer/card arrival, approval, chunk custody, receipt, complete local bytes and OS save are distinct. Conversation receive policy can override the default. Approved ordinary downloads save after completion to the configured or system Downloads folder. Message Yourself and linked devices can synchronize cards separately from attachment bytes. Group sources still need authorization, retained bytes, a reachable path and sharing permission. [File flow](../docs/network-design-reference.md#e-files-folders-consent-and-completion) · [Custody](../docs/network-design-reference.md#ordinary-file-custody) · [Receiving help](../docs/help/topics/send-files.md) · [File ceiling](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/node.rs#L38) · [Chunk size](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/file/crypto.rs#L40) · [Directory limits](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/file/directory.rs#L14)
- **Ownership and candidates.** Core \`file/\`, \`files.rs\`, filebook, consent and completion own correctness. The intake hook, composer and files tray own user interaction. Rely on the existing status paths before proposing a new receipt. Test online handoff, approval after sender restart, alternate source or evicted custody, an excluded account, and bytes saved versus a card alone. A transfer-readiness or recovery-navigation improvement is a candidate if observation shows confusion. Repeated approvals, large-transfer throughput/pause/resume, fast selection of several known recipients and extra storage are separate candidates with distinct costs and authority. REQ-028 covered optional file/forum/cache contribution incentives while protecting basic chat. Historical network evidence already includes a consented no-direct-route transfer and physical byte verification. [Module owners](../docs/module-boundaries.md#L85) · [Delivery help](../docs/help/topics/delivery.md) · [Evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)

## 3. Groups, ephemeral rooms and anonymity

- **At HEAD.** New desktop groups grant membership and owner roles to verified accounts. Invitation pending gives metadata visibility until acceptance. Certified siblings inherit accepted membership and receive their own keys. Owner controls include rename, announcement, ownership transfer, removal and dissolution. Leave/rejoin uses distinct grant lifetimes. Removal advances key authority and a new grant requires fresh acceptance. Dissolution leaves read-only local history. Personal conversation removal has its own optional local cleanup and keeps other accounts' copies outside its authority. Current announcements and photos have separate revisions and authorization from previous chat history. Bounded owner-selected text history is an explicit pre-join exception. Legacy device-only groups need the owner-authorized migration and can remain pending when an original device is offline. [Group network authority](../docs/network-design-reference.md#d-group-creation-distribution-and-member-recovery) · [Channel lifecycle](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#L214) · [Channels help](../docs/help/topics/channels.md) · [Local removal owner](../docs/module-boundaries.md#L93)
- **Privacy boundary.** Member presentation uses nickname/avatar/role per verified account. Invisible mode limits public discovery and uses local reply permissions while existing group access remains. Relay mailbox pseudonyms minimize metadata and still expose connection identity, mailbox correlation, size buckets and timing. Existing message expiry is a message-granularity deadline. These paths supply no anonymous participation or expiring-room contract. The separate REQ-019/024 forum expiry and pinning concept never supplied a group-chat policy. [Privacy controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md#network-privacy-and-contact-lists) · [Relay metadata boundary](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md#L61) · [Expiring messages](../docs/help/topics/delivery.md#expiring-messages)
- **Candidate slices.** REQ-018 belongs with the group authority and reception owners. Qualify announcement race/pending UX apart from membership changes. A temporary private room can build on signed membership if product chooses a single lifetime, expiry/leave behavior, host exit and retained-copy disclosure. Pseudonymous presentation or anonymous admission needs a distinct REQ-013/025 threat and abuse decision covering peer, LAN, relay and moderator observability, rejoin/linkability, access removal, and previously copied content. Define evidence around pending invitation, partitioned removal, owner transfer and retained history. Group/anonymous rooms remain separable from group voice. [Group reception](../docs/group-conversation-reception.md) · [Group ownership](../docs/module-boundaries.md#L79)

## 4. Identity, trust and linked devices

- **At HEAD.** Local sign-in/profile storage, account identity, and device signing/key-agreement identity are distinct. UI names/avatars and discovery are hints. Manual safety-number comparison records verification privately. Current linking uses a one-time 128-bit code bound to the exact device and an authenticated live direct route, with durable enrollment, session invalidation and restricted recovery after interrupted adoption. Sibling replay is category-selectable and needs an eligible reachable source. Directory presence and relay mailboxes cannot carry pairing or full sibling replay. Device-local settings such as OS permissions and download paths remain separate. [Glossary](../CONTEXT.md) · [Contact verification](../docs/peer-trust.md#private-verification) · [Pairing and replay](../docs/network-design-reference.md#L1789) · [Account and device decisions](../docs/multi-device-sync-design.md#account-and-device-decision-boundaries)
- **Recovery and authority.** Encrypted manual backup preserves the account fingerprint and creates a new device. Old device keys and live ratchets are excluded. Restored group history begins as an archive. The architecture allows a certified sibling to supply account-grant inheritance for a compatible group and documents legacy migration as a separate boundary. The backup help describes owner reinvitation broadly, so verify the exact certified/unlinked and legacy/current paths before changing restore UX. Compromised-device revocation with the same identity remains a future authority protocol because linked devices share account signing authority. Removing a device from a view or changing sync selection cannot retire that secret. New-identity recovery is the documented path after suspected compromise. [Backup help](../docs/backup-recovery.md#restore-after-losing-a-device) · [Restore architecture](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#L2760) · [Future account authority](../docs/multi-device-sync-design.md#future-account-authority-v2)
- **Candidate slices.** REQ-010 covered a user-triggered QR action in chat image/preview with explicit result review. It did not settle contact/URL/plain-text formats. A contact QR UX can reuse current binding and verification owners. Treat matching proof, secure pairing and contact permission as separate outcomes. REQ-025 practical stranger/abuse work should use core admission. Hidden contacts and contact deletion are presentation/history controls. Endorsements and identity-preserving revocation are independent higher-cost decisions. [Identity/linking owners](../docs/module-boundaries.md#L74) · [Privacy and contact controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md#network-privacy-and-contact-lists)

## 5. Offline transport and topology

- **At HEAD.** Peers can use an existing reachable LAN without internet. Signed multicast discovery and bounded unicast hints locate endpoints for identity-pinned Noise/TCP. Manual probe and existing routed paths, including supported Tailscale/EasyTier inventory, cover additional reachable endpoints. Offline recipient delivery is direct-first with optional trusted post-office custody/federation, or authorized group-member recovery. A 30-day maximum and capacity eviction bound custody. The relay store has a 512 MiB ciphertext cap, so the file input ceiling does not predict offline capacity. A preferred or alternate relay needs its own surviving onward route. Discovery, routing, consent/admission, custody and verified recipient receipt all have their own evidence. Two isolated networks with no usable IP or relay route retain their separate islands. [Topology matrix](../docs/network-topologies.md#topology-scenarios) · [Privacy gates](../docs/privacy-controls.md#network-privacy-and-contact-lists) · [Relay retention](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md#L108) · [Delivery help](../docs/help/topics/delivery.md)
- **Experimental radio.** Commit \`4538da2f\` (#342) added a native BLE rehearsal. A Rust bounded byte stream and macOS CoreBluetooth helper carry pinned Noise for a two-host encrypted echo. The documented path has no chat delivery or Bitchat interoperability. No runtime BLE chat integration or LoRa transport surfaced in the inspected source. No-IP operation, internet-less but working LAN, recipient offline and a partition are four different acceptance scenarios. [BLE owner and limits](../docs/native-bluetooth.md#ownership-and-authentication) · [Desktop integration boundary](../docs/native-bluetooth.md#desktop-integration-boundary)
- **Candidate slices.** First evaluate the existing offline file handoff on a LAN with internet disabled, a recipient temporarily offline and a visible excluded account. Measure which source restores delivery, file completeness, user steps and failure clarity. Pursue native fallback only for a verified no-IP scenario with an explicit target platform, privacy/admission and bounded transport lifecycle. Require two real hosts, connection interruption, radio permission and resume evidence. Cross-site data needs a separately tested surviving topology. [Physical network evidence](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)

## 6. Web and PWA

- **At HEAD.** React is the desktop shell over Tauri IPC. The committed GitHub Pages workflow publishes \`site/\` plus generated user help, and the local agent HTTP adapter is fixed-route loopback with browser-origin rejection. The inspected HEAD tree has no production browser messenger, PWA service worker or recipient review portal. A browser harness exercising frontend behavior and public site uptime are separate from client acceptance. [Tauri messaging adapter](../frontend/src/lib/api/chat.ts#L1) · [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L1) · [Local agent HTTP boundary](../docs/bot-integrations.md#L247)
- **Separate committed prototype.** Local tracking ref \`origin/feature/mobile-pwa\` is \`1cd7e78e\` (2026-10-11), with a merge base of \`0d7ae04b\`. Its feature commit \`26d7c68a\` adds a narrow browser shell, service worker, WASM browser node and WebSocket signaling to a desktop gateway that remains in the data path. WebRTC DataChannel carries Noise and uses host ICE. The branch notes record origin-bound IndexedDB identity, stale IP/QR bootstrap, secure-context and WSS barriers, foreground-only sync, incomplete existing-account adoption, unpinned first-contact gateway, credential storage, role/start order and misleading success issues. The older Chromium and build artifacts described there do not establish a real-phone DM round trip. The Android record describes a native direction without an APK build. Inspect locally with \`git show 1cd7e78e:docs/mobile-pwa-feasibility.md\` (lines 13–61 and 91–103) and \`git show 1cd7e78e:docs/android-apk-readiness.md\` (lines 1–25).
- **Candidate slices.** REQ-002 (WORK-14/T041–T043) is no-install viewing and comments through link or link+code. Start with one content type and scoped read/revocation. Product and host owners then settle comments, revisions, host-offline behavior and permissions. Editing remains later. REQ-027 (WORK-19/T047–T050) covers a separate mobile encrypted client and authorized own/post-office nodes. A first decision needs platform, stable start origin, authenticated QR/device binding, key ownership and foreground/offline promises. Test one real phone and two physical desktops with end-to-end replies through the gateway, changed IP and restored session before adding authorized multi-node failover. Native Android distribution and browser/PWA delivery each need their own acceptance. The prototype is local evidence for historical behavior, with no fresh remote PR/owner or browser-platform verification in this audit.

## 7. Clipboard, OCR and translation

- **At HEAD.** The composer stages pasted files/images for explicit Send through the same attachment intake used by the picker and drop. Screenshot confirmation copies and stages the final PNG. Text and whole-image copies use separate helpers under the local sensitive-copy confirmation and best-effort clear policy. Supported macOS Live Text can copy selected text from an ordinary image. Protected images disallow copy and text selection. The inspected current paths expose no cross-device clipboard history, background capture or message translation. [Composer paste](../frontend/src/features/chat/Composer.tsx#L510) · [Attachment owner](../docs/module-boundaries.md#L925) · [Sensitive text clipboard](../frontend/src/lib/sensitiveClipboard.ts) · [Image clipboard](../frontend/src/lib/imageClipboard.ts) · [Image actions](../docs/help/topics/send-files.md#image-actions)
- **Language boundary.** The eight interface locales and display formatting are presentation. Architecture documents that the language can travel with optional appearance sync. Core content restrictions and bundled language models were explicitly removed in \`f728e188\` (#243) after \`0ca641d7\`. The compatibility decoder keeps old signed data readable without republishing the removed policy. Translation is a new feature decision. [Language help](../docs/help/topics/language.md#change-the-display-language) · [Retired language contract](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#retired-profile-and-snapshot-metadata) · [Compatibility regression](../crates/mesh-talk-core/src/node/unrestricted_messages_tests.rs)
- **Candidate slices.** Trial an explicit one-shot clipboard handoff via Message Yourself before opening any background sync or clipboard history design. Set preview, permitted data formats, protected-content enforcement, lock/revocation behavior and conflict handling up front. For translation, decide on-device versus explicit provider disclosure, language and size limits, scope for protected content and retention. Keep the original message visible and preserve its signed text. Validate denied clipboard permission, stale write after lock or session change, and unavailable translation provider. [Linked state ownership](../docs/multi-device-sync-design.md#private-state-replication) · [Clipboard/privacy controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md)

## 8. Desktop, relay and deployment

- **At HEAD.** The exact-source release workflow targets macOS, Windows and Linux on x86-64 and ARM64. Stable is an explicitly verified tagged publication and Nightly is sourced from trusted main. Signed one-click updating covers installed macOS bundles, Windows NSIS and Linux AppImage with required updater artifacts. Source builds, MSI and DEB/RPM use the manual path. Desktop installers and standalone post-office archives are separate. Windows offers a boot Scheduled Task and macOS a boot LaunchDaemon. The Linux amd64/arm64 relay image uses host-network Linux Docker plus persistent private identity/data and password storage. Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows has a different LAN multicast boundary. The public Pages site distributes downloads/help. Optional Google Drive is a user-triggered encrypted backup destination in a configured desktop build. [Release targets](../.github/workflows/release.yml#L80) · [Updater support](../docs/updates.md#one-click-installation) · [Stable gates](../docs/updates.md#stable-promotion-and-acceptance) · [Relay packages](../docs/post-office-release.md) · [Drive backup](../docs/backup-recovery.md#google-drive-backup-and-restore)
- **Candidate slices.** REQ-014/M04 belongs with release packaging. Compare identical artifact role, OS, architecture and format with the last verified package and measure installed footprint separately. Installer, updater signing, native installation and restart remain independent evidence. For deployment usability, first qualify a standalone relay install/backup/update and discovery on the target OS and topology. Managed hosting, browser gateways, Android APK/installability and general remote-access services need independent product and operations ownership. Reuse the separate peer-operated relay model for bounded custody where it fits. [Size owner](../docs/updates.md#manual-package-size-budgets) · [Deployment guide](../specifications/deployment_guide.md) · [Version ownership](../docs/updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle)

Saved the [REQ-029 product baseline and candidate backlog](/Users/kingsonwu/programming/OctopusGarage/mesh-talk/.worktrees/req-029/tmp/req-029-product-baseline.md). It covers all eight requested areas at commit `0ae1a692`, with 73 verified local source links and historical requirement ownership.

- Offline delivery depends on a reachable, authorized source that still holds the data. The BLE path is a two-host macOS rehearsal, and the mobile PWA lives on a separate prototype branch.
- The notes identify an internet-disconnected LAN file handoff as a bounded first scenario for REQ-029. It can show where existing behavior meets the need and where users struggle to recover a transfer.

This was a source audit. No builds, runtime tests, code edits, or commits. The tracked worktree is clean.
